question: At 12 states under 5% reading noise, does replacing the per-B fresh UNSAT chain and the separate B_max confirmation with one incremental SAT instance per step (flip variables summed by a totalizer; budgets set by assumptions on the totalizer outputs, learned clauses kept across budgets and across steps) bring the capped queries under the 9 s timer, so that the sound stop from A12 keeps WRONG 0 while recovering identifications?
motivation: Study 037 (Observed): the sound stop removed the 036 least-B WRONG (GSAFE12 Exact: the sealed 036 trace now gives AMB) but the B_max confirmation query timed out on 10/12 clean12 cases (e.g. 10330001 at 9.0 s) and 5/12 noisy12 cases for A12_r5, and on 9/12 noisy8 cases for A12_r3, turning ID into IDU. Upward doubling halved first-probe caps (6/12 vs 12/12) but did not move IDU. Inferred: each budget and each confirmation rebuilds and re-solves a near-identical CNF from scratch; the cost is the repeated encoding and lost learning, not the budget order

arms.A13_r5: new file brute/scalesearch13.py: A12 (frozen scalesearch12) logic with r = 5, B_max(5) = 2. One change: per step, a single incremental CNF over the fused trace with one flip variable per read position, a totalizer over the flip variables, and budgets enforced by assumptions on the totalizer outputs. Least-B: assume <= 0, 1, 2, ... upward until SAT (unit increments, since each probe reuses the instance). Confirmation: same instance plus the start-state-distinct rival clauses guarded by an activation literal, under assumption <= B_max. Learned clauses persist across budgets and across steps (clauses only added as the trace grows). Stop rule and labels identical to A12
